Real, trimmed (3-period) JSON-stat 2.0 responses fetched live 2026-07-28.
Each file is named by its Eurostat dataset code (the same code
config/series/*.yaml's source_refs[].ref carries) so tests can derive the
dataset dynamically from the fixture filename/path, never as a Go string
literal (app/internal/guard's origin-identifier deny-list already forbids
"prc_hicp_minr", "une_rt_q", "nama_10_gdp", "coicop", "coicop18" as Go
literals outside /config and testdata/).

Trimming: each file keeps every field the decoder actually reads
(version, class, label, source, updated, value, id, size, dimension) and
drops Eurostat's large "extension"/"status" metadata blocks (dataset
description, DOI/annotation history, footnote links) that the adapter
does not parse — the kept fields are byte-real, not fabricated.

prc_hicp_minr.json
  URL: https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/prc_hicp_minr?format=JSON&lang=EN&freq=M&geo=ES&unit=RCH_A&coicop18=TOTAL&lastTimePeriod=3
  Fetched: 2026-07-28. HTTP 200. 3 periods: 2026-04=3.5, 2026-05=3.6, 2026-06=3.6.
  2026-06=3.6 independently matches the prompt's separately stated verified
  fact for this series/period.

une_rt_q.json
  URL: https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/une_rt_q?format=JSON&lang=EN&freq=Q&geo=ES&s_adj=SA&age=Y15-74&unit=PC_ACT&sex=T&lastTimePeriod=3
  Fetched: 2026-07-28. HTTP 200. 3 periods: 2025-Q3=10.5, 2025-Q4=10.2, 2026-Q1=10.3.

nama_10_gdp.json
  URL: https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/nama_10_gdp?format=JSON&lang=EN&freq=A&geo=ES&unit=CLV10_MEUR&na_item=B1GQ&lastTimePeriod=3
  Fetched: 2026-07-28. HTTP 200. 3 periods: 2023=1239392.8, 2024=1282216.9, 2025=1318439.0.

deadcode/prc_hicp_minr-coicop18-cp00.json
  URL: https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/prc_hicp_minr?format=JSON&lang=EN&freq=M&geo=ES&unit=RCH_A&coicop18=CP00&lastTimePeriod=3
  Fetched: 2026-07-28. HTTP 200, 4481 bytes. Task 6.10/6.11's dead-code
  fixture: "CP00" is the ECOICOP v1 all-items code, discontinued since
  ECOICOP ver.2 (the live all-items code is "TOTAL" — see
  config/series/ipc-armonizado-eurostat.yaml's own doc comment and spec
  source-ingestion-eurostat, "In ECOICOP ver.2 the all-items code is
  TOTAL; CP00 is the dead v1 code"). Requesting it returns HTTP 200 (not
  an HTTP error — this is the whole point: a dead identifier is not a
  transport failure) with "size":[1,1,0,1,3] (the coicop18 dimension has
  ZERO categories) and "value":{} (structurally empty). Kept in its own
  subdirectory (testdata/deadcode/, not testdata/) so it is never picked
  up by loadEurostatFixtures's "exactly 3 real datasets" glob in
  client_test.go.

sparse/nama_10_gdp-full-history.json
  URL: https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/api/dissemination/statistics/1.0/data/nama_10_gdp?format=JSON&lang=EN&freq=A&unit=CLV10_MEUR&na_item=B1GQ&geo=ES
  Fetched: 2026-07-30. HTTP 200, 4689 bytes on the wire. The FULL history
  (no lastTimePeriod), i.e. exactly the request config/series/pib-eurostat.yaml
  drives in production — and exactly the payload that produced the reported
  "observation_check" constraint violation at pib-eurostat/1975.
  Trimmed the same way as the three files above: only Eurostat's unparsed
  "extension" block is dropped; "value", "status", "id", "size" and the whole
  "dimension" tree are byte-real (every one of the 31 numeric value tokens was
  checked to appear verbatim in the original body).
  Shape that makes it worth keeping: "size":[1,1,1,1,51] — the time dimension
  declares 51 annual periods, 1975..2025, while "value" carries only 31
  entries, positions 20..50 (1995..2025). The 20 leading positions 0..19
  (1975..1994) carry NO value: Eurostat's time dimension spans further back
  than the data. This is the SPARSENESS every JSON-stat response has, and the
  reason a valueless position must yield no observation rather than a
  nil-valued one (envelope.go's value-presence branch; sparse_test.go).
  It is also the only checked-in fixture carrying a REAL "status" map:
  {"48":"p","49":"p","50":"p"} — 2023/2024/2025 are provisional.
  Kept in its own subdirectory (testdata/sparse/, not testdata/) so it is
  never picked up by loadEurostatFixtures's "exactly 3 real datasets" glob in
  client_test.go, following testdata/deadcode/'s precedent.

Sparseness verified live 2026-07-30 across all three configured datasets, with
the same full-history (no lastTimePeriod) requests config/series/*.yaml issue:

  nama_10_gdp    51 declared periods, 31 values, 20 valueless (1975..1994)
  une_rt_q       93 declared periods, 69 values, 24 valueless (2003-Q1..2008-Q4)
  prc_hicp_minr 366 declared periods, 354 values, 12 valueless (1996-01..1996-12)

In all three the valueless positions form ONE CONTIGUOUS LEADING HEAD — there
are no interior holes — so dropping them leaves a dense, step-1 history and the
cadence audit (indicators.AssertCadence, design D-4) classifies the same
periodicity it did before. Also checked in all three: ZERO positions carry a
"status" entry without a "value" entry, so the fail-closed
flag-on-a-valueless-position branch costs nothing against today's real data.

Also verified live (not checked in as a fixture, reported in the apply-progress
transcript instead): the SAME three base URLs without lastTimePeriod each
return HTTP 200 with every non-time dimension fully pinned (freq/unit/
coicop18/geo for prc_hicp_minr; freq/s_adj/age/unit/sex/geo for une_rt_q;
freq/unit/na_item/geo for nama_10_gdp) and reasonable sizes (20259 / 7442 /
4689 bytes respectively) — confirming the URL shape works against the real
endpoint, not only against these trimmed httptest fixtures (the PR 5b
lesson: a fixture server answers whatever URL it is asked, so URL
correctness — including that `freq` must be pinned like every other
non-time dimension — was checked against the live service before relying
on it here).
